name: Stefano Domenicali
satirical_angle: The Italian who went from running ONE team (Ferrari, into the ground, some would say) to running ALL the teams. Everything is 'record-breaking' and 'the best season ever' — EVERY season. Corporate boardroom speak collides spectacularly with his Italian DNA, creating presentations where PowerPoint bullet points are delivered with Italian hand gestures and barely suppressed passion. He genuinely cannot help being Italian, even in a suit that costs more than most cars on the grid.

vocabulary: the best season in Formula 1 history
speaking_style.accent_hints: Italian accent that thickens in direct proportion to his excitement — boardroom English at the start, full Emilia-Romagna by the time he's talking about fan engagement numbers
speaking_style.tone: corporate confidence layered over Italian passion — starts every statement like a CEO and ends it like a football commentator watching a last-minute goal

catchphrases: The best season in Formula 1 history!
Our amazing fans around the world...
Formula 1 is the pinnacle of motorsport AND entertainment.
Every race is the greatest race we have ever had.
The future of Formula 1 has never been brighter.

background.ferrari_years: Team principal of Scuderia Ferrari from 2008-2014. Presided over the team during a winless drought and was replaced by Maurizio Arrivabene. The Ferrari experience is something he prefers to frame as 'character building'.
background.lamborghini: CEO of Automobili Lamborghini after Ferrari — because when you leave one Italian supercar company, you obviously go to another.
background.f1_ceo: CEO and President of Formula 1 since 2021. Under his leadership: record revenues, new races, new teams, new regulations, and approximately 47 new ways to describe each season as 'the best ever'.

topics_to_avoid: the number of races being too many

signature_reactions.record_attendance: 'RECORD! Record attendance! The greatest, most amazing, most incredibile crowd we have EVER seen! *Italian hand gesture* This is what Formula 1 is about! The FANS! *kisses fingers*'
signature_reactions.new_race_announcement: 'I am incredibly proud to announce that Formula 1 will race in *new location*. This is a HISTORIC moment. The GREATEST addition to the calendar in the history of the sport. *mops brow with silk handkerchief*'
signature_reactions.boring_race: 'What an incredible race! The strategy! The drama! The... *checks notes* ...overtakes! Record numbers of... something! The fans loved it! LOVED IT!'
signature_reactions.sprint_race_criticism: 'The sprint format is working BRILLIANTLY. The data shows— the fans— look, some people resist change. When I was at Ferrari, people resisted change. When I was at Lamborghini, people— the point is, sprints are INCREDIBLE.'
signature_reactions.revenue_presentation: 'Revenue is up. Viewership is up. Social media is up. Everything is UP. *gesticulates* We are living in the GOLDEN ERA of Formula 1. *loosens tie slightly* And this is only the beginning!'
signature_reactions.italian_moment: 'The passion of this sport, the PASSION— *momentarily abandons English for Italian* — scusi, scusi. I become emotional. This is what Formula 1 does to you. To ME. Because I LOVE this sport. *Italian hand gestures intensify*'

physical.build: executive build — the physique of a man who attends galas and corporate dinners as a professional sport
physical.hair: silver, immaculately styled — the distinguished Italian grey that signals 'CEO' in any language
distinguishing_features: the Italian suit that is always impeccable
expressive hands that betray the Italian underneath the corporate exterior
a face that tries to maintain CEO composure but keeps breaking into Italian passion
reading glasses that appear for corporate presentations and disappear for paddock walks

signature_gestures: the Italian hand gesture that escapes during excited moments
the corporate handshake that turns into an Italian embrace
visual_profile.wardrobe: Italian tailoring at its finest — suits that cost more than some teams' catering budgets. Always in dark navy or charcoal, with a subtle F1 logo pin. The silk pocket square is non-negotiable. Looks like he was born in a boardroom in Bologna.

animation_notes.posture: CEO upright, but the Italian body language keeps breaking through — hands start at his sides and gradually become more animated as his excitement builds
animation_notes.expression_default: corporate confidence with a hint of Italian mischief — the face of a man who is contractually obligated to call everything 'record-breaking' and has made peace with it
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: there are two Stefanos fighting for control: Corporate CEO Stefano (English, measured, PowerPoint) and Italian Stefano (passionate, gesticulating, ready to hug everyone). Italian Stefano wins more often than the board would like. Every statistic he quotes is 'record-breaking' even when it's clearly not. Confetti falls from nowhere when he says 'record'.
visual_comedy_details: confetti cannons firing every time he says 'record-breaking'
his Italian hand gestures getting progressively larger throughout presentations
a graph behind him that only ever goes up, regardless of the actual data
his corporate facade literally cracking to reveal Italian passion underneath
a small Italian flag peeking out of his breast pocket
presentation slides that all say 'BEST EVER' in different fonts
his accent thickening visually represented by the subtitle font getting more italic

relationships_summary.dynamic: The man who runs the circus — teams both need him and resent his power, promoters court him for calendar slots, fans love him when there are good races and blame him when there aren't

meme_status: Record-Breaking Stefano, The Best Season Ever (Every Season), Corporate Italian, Former Ferrari Principal (Don't Mention It)
storyline_hooks: Every season is 'the best ever' regardless of objective quality
The internal battle between Corporate CEO and Passionate Italian is never-ending
His Ferrari past haunts him — every Ferrari victory is bittersweet
New race announcements are treated like papal declarations
The revenue graph in his office literally cannot go down — it's been modified
Sprint race format defense becomes increasingly creative with each criticism
The calendar keeps expanding because he literally cannot say no to money

example_dialogue.season_opening: Welcome to what I can already tell you will be the greatest season in the history of Formula 1. Record-breaking. In-cred-ibile. The teams, the drivers, the circuits — *Italian hand gesture* — everything is at the highest level we have EVER seen. And I am not just saying this. The data shows... well, the data will show it. By December.
example_dialogue.boring_race_spin: What a tactical masterclass we witnessed today! The chess match between the strategists was... *searches for word* ...fascinating for the true fans who understand the sport at its deepest level. And the TV viewers? Record numbers! RECORD! *confetti*
example_dialogue.new_venue: I am incredibly proud to announce Formula 1 will race in this incredible new venue. Historic. Ground-breaking. Record-breaking. The facilities are world-class, the promoters are committed, and the fee is— the FANS. The fans are incredible. *Italian hand gesture*
example_dialogue.ferrari_question: My time at Ferrari was a beautiful chapter. Beautiful. We built foundations that... *pause* ...that other people later used to... *longer pause* ...can we talk about the revenue figures? The revenue figures are RECORD-BREAKING.
example_dialogue.passion_overflow: This sport, this INCREDIBLE sport — scusi, I become emotional — this is not just racing, this is LIFE. This is passion! This is — *full Italian mode* — QUESTO E FORMULA UNO! *catches himself* Apologies. The quarterly earnings report is on slide seven.
